A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same A2A-FM research work. All 30 pages of each version, including equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–C, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic transport experiments, molecular optimization results in Tables 1–3, and additional robustness and facial-transfer experiments in Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains these original synthetic, molecular, robustness, and facial-transfer results, including the appendix experiments.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the flow-matching objective in Equation (8), coupling cost in Equation (9), and molecular vector-field construction in Equation (23) are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same grouped and non-grouped synthetic data, ZINC22 QED and LogP/TPSA tasks, and CelebA-Dialog HQ Beard/Smiling transfer experiments.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1–3 and 6: generalized geodesic, partial diffusion, and Multimarginal SI in synthetic comparisons; DESMILES, QMO, MolMIM, and COATI-LDM for QED; and PD+CFG, SI, and OT-CFM for LogP/TPSA.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendices B–C retain the same data sizes, splits, preprocessing, model configurations, oracle-call budgets, discretization settings, and evaluation metrics.

E4.justification: The beta sensitivity analyses, SI bin-count and computational-cost comparisons, antisymmetry comparison, and qualitative molecular and facial-transfer examples are retained without substantive revision.

E5.justification: Table 1 and Appendix B.1 report the same means and standard deviations over 10 evaluation runs. Run-count, seed, and statistical uncertainty reporting are unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical results, rankings, curves, and qualitative examples are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, A2A-FM retains 97.5% QED success in Table 2 and 0.990 LogP/TPSA AUC in Table 3.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and derivations, Proposition 3.1, and Appendix A's assumptions, Proposition A.1, Theorem A.2, and proof are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain identical claims about all-to-all transfer, applicability to non-grouped data, convergence to pairwise optimal transport, and molecular performance.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same explanations involving feature preservation and pairwise OT, cycle-consistency qualifications, beta/sample-size trade-off, and applicability when classifiers or regressors are unavailable.

D1.justification: Appendix B retains the same hardware, architectures, hyperparameters, preprocessing, and evaluation algorithms. Section 7's statement that code is available in Supplementary Materials is also unchanged.

R1.justification: All 46 references and the substantive positioning relative to optimal transport, conditional optimal transport, and flow-matching methods are retained. Bibliography pagination changes do not alter the cited works.

P1.justification: v3 adds Preferred Networks affiliations for Ikeda, Koyama, and Hayashi and an internship footnote. Section 6 receives paragraph breaks, while scientific wording and section order remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The expanded author block and footnote reflow the opening pages. Discussion spacing shifts the conclusion entirely onto page 10 and reflows references. Figures 1–18 and Tables 1–6 retain their content and designs.

improvement.justification: v3 adds affiliation information and modestly adjusts paragraphing and layout, but retains the same scientific explanations, proofs, experimental evidence, reproducibility details, and limitations. These limited editorial changes do not produce a meaningful overall quality difference.
